note: Every enquiry this archive has sent, what came back, and what is still owed. It existed in three places — prose on the open-questions page, entries in the research log, and drafts in a folder — and no one of them showed what was outstanding. A PUBLISHED ADDRESS THAT BOUNCES IS WORSE THAN NO ADDRESS: every enquirer is sending into it and none of them knows.

rows.what: The same six bound estate files — what she charges and how, her own view of whether the work is worth doing, and an offer to begin with one
rows.back: THE FIRST PAID-RESEARCH APPROACH THIS PROJECT HAS MADE. Everything before it went to an institution and waited. No payment details were sent and none will be: the letter asks her to name her own arrangement.

DELIBERATELY NOT SENT. The National Archives' own record gives pmbarchives@dact.kzntl.gov.za on an entry last touched in 2015 and kzntl.gov.za is a retired domain; other listings give pmbarchives@kzndac.gov.za. The postal address and the telephone agree everywhere. This archive has already posted one enquiry into a mailbox it could not confirm. 15 SEPTEMBER, AND THE REASON FOR HOLDING IT IS WEAKER THAN IT WAS: both domains ACCEPT MAIL. kzndac.gov.za and dact.kzntl.gov.za each have MX records and no website, which is an ordinary shape for a government department. A domain taking mail and a person reading the mailbox are different facts, so telephoning first is still the better plan — but “almost certainly dead” was more than the evidence supported.

rows.what: WO 97 and WO 12 for the 21st Light Dragoons — the discharge paper that would give James Mountjoy his parish of birth
rows.back: Raised 15 September, on one sentence in a newspaper. The first errand this archive has had outside South Africa. 15 SEPTEMBER — AND IT CANNOT BE POSTED AS AN EMAIL. The National Archives take records and research enquiries THROUGH A WEB FORM and publish no enquiry address; the domain has a mailbox but no address anybody is invited to write to. This archive does not send letters into mailboxes it cannot confirm — it has said so about Pietermaritzburg for two days and will not make an exception for itself. The letter is written and waiting on a decision about the form.

rows.what: Guidance on tracing James Mountjoy, a saddler discharged from the 21st Dragoons (Light) at the Cape about 1816 — which series after WO 97, and whether WO 12/1430 is the musters to read
rows.back: DRAFTED AFTER SEARCHING, NOT INSTEAD OF IT. Discovery was searched for four spellings across the WO series: the name-catalogued discharge series hold two Montjoys and neither is this man. The control says the absence is real — 95 WO 97 records for “21st Dragoons (Light)” in a single page — so the letter asks whether the reading is right (pensioners' papers would not hold a man discharged at the Cape without a pension) and points at WO 12/1430 and the WO 25 description books. 15 SEPTEMBER — AND IT CANNOT BE POSTED AS AN EMAIL. rows.to: National Library of South Africa, Special Collections, Cape Town
rows.what: MSB751, the GA Kolbe Collection — a copy of the letter of 23 August 1830 from Johan Kolbe in London to his son on his ordination, and whether it carries a London address
rows.back: SENT 15 September to specialcollections@nlsa.ac.za, after checking that the domain takes mail. A DIFFERENT BUILDING FROM THE ONE THIS ARCHIVE KEEPS WRITING TO: the library at 5 Queen Victoria Street, not the archives at 72 Roeland Street. It asks for the letter of 23 August 1830, for whether it carries a London address at its head, and for two things about the item itself — where the original is, since the catalogue calls this a photocopy, and whether “LMS missionary” comes from the papers or from the donor. THAT LAST QUESTION IS THE ONE THAT MATTERS MOST: the only other evidence for his mission work is a recollection written down forty-five years later, and whether the two are independent witnesses or one family memory told twice is the difference between corroboration and an echo.
